_note: The trainer scouting report's editable settings (docs/TRAINER_REPORT.md). Every threshold and list the engine uses lives here, not in code. Steps 2-4 add the matrix verdicts, bulk threshold, slider signals and tags.

lens._note: Gen IV is the primary lens: a version names its game, and that game's data (type chart, typing, stats, abilities, learnsets) is used.

level_scale._note: Every row's stats are computed at this level unless a build records its own. Change it to read teams at another level.

defaults._note: What a build gets when it leaves a field open. The report lists every default it used. Cartridge trainers keep the game's values (no EVs, their difficulty-scaled IVs).

validation._note: Move legality is biological (D-048): a move counts if the species can learn it in any game of any generation, or uses it in the show, or the build records a reason. The report states the reason; only a move with no reason at all is flagged.

slider_scale._note: Authored sliders run 0-100. The left pole is 0, the right pole is 100.

verdicts._note: How a type-chart multiplier becomes a word. Checked in order: the first rule that fits wins. Abilities rewrite the multiplier first.

abilities._note: Abilities that rewrite a matchup before the verdict: {ability: {attacking type: multiplier}}. 'super_effective' scales only super-effective hits; 'not_super_effective' replaces every hit that isn't. A Pokémon only gets an ability its species could have in that generation.

bulk._note: A row's bulk lean, from its real stats. Physical bulk is HP x Defense, special bulk is HP x Sp. Def; HP cancels out, so the test compares Defense with Sp. Def. If one is lower than the other by at least the threshold, the row is soft on that side.

team._note: The team summary, from the attacker's side. A gap is a type that hits this team hard; a strength is a type this team handles.

signals._note: How the engine measures each slider from the team's data, to check the authored value. Every signal is a share of the team (0-100): how many members show it. A slider's measured value is the average of its signals that have data; a signal with no data on the team is left out, and a slider with none says 'no signal'. Weights are equal unless set. Missing data is never evidence: a member with no item recorded doesn't count for or against Choice items; a plain ball, no ribbons or no nickname say nothing about bond.

attack_heavy.label: attack-heavy stats
attack_heavy.rule: best attacking stat is higher than the average of its two defenses

damage_moves.label: mostly attacks
damage_moves.rule: at least this many of its moves deal damage

fast.label: fast
fast.rule: Speed at or above the median fully evolved Pokémon of its generation, same level and defaults

narrow_evs.label: narrow EV spreads
narrow_evs.rule: at least this share of its EVs in two stats (only builds with recorded EVs)

few_attack_types.label: low move-type variety
few_attack_types.rule: its attacks cover at most this many types

ball.label: a partner's ball (Luxury, Friend, Heal, Cherish, Premier)

risky.label: carries a gamble
risky.rule: a move under this accuracy, a one-hit KO move, recoil, a self-KO move, or one of these items

disagreement._note: When the measured value is at least this far from the authored one, the report notes it and names the signals behind it.

nature_clash._note: A nature that pulls against its trainer gets a line. Each rule: a slider and a side ('high' at or above 'at', 'low' at or below it), and the nature stats that clash. Only builds with a recorded nature are read.

rules.line: {species} has a {nature} nature: built to take hits, on a trainer who wants to deal them.
{species} has a {nature} nature: built to hit hard, on a trainer who'd rather absorb first.
{species} has a {nature} nature, trading bulk for power: a gamble on a percentage player's team.

tags._note: Badges: simple rules that fire on thresholds. A tag earns its place only if it changes a line of the report (tested).

cohesive.name: Cohesive
cohesive.rule: at least this many members share a move

type_dominant.name: Type-dominant
type_dominant.rule: at least this many members share a type
